factual_methodological.summary: Same-day Eurostat inflation data, ECB policy rates, Japan Statistics Bureau labour data and MHLW vacancy data were checked against primary releases. U.S. JOLTS is used only as the latest available labour-flow baseline, and the September Employment Situation is explicitly excluded because it falls after the information cutoff.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The brief is organized around inflation persistence, labour-demand momentum and policy divergence rather than a release-by-release list. Stocks and flows are distinguished, cross-country inflation dispersion is qualified, and the U.S. leg remains explicitly unresolved.

novelty_against_previous_daily.summary: The lead shifts materially from 1 October U.S. manufacturing cost pressure to 2 October euro-area inflation reacceleration, Japanese vacancy-flow softening and the pre-payroll U.S. labour setup.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 Markdown table + 3 explicit charts + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Quantitative visuals reproduce values from the cited primary releases and preserve EN/PT-BR parity; the causal chain is framed as a risk mechanism rather than proven causality.

political_neutrality.summary: Central-bank policy trade-offs are described without endorsement, opposition, scoring or ranking.

contrary_evidence: Euro-area inflation acceleration is heavily influenced by energy; non-energy industrial-goods inflation eased from 1.2% to 1.1%.
Japan's active job-openings-to-applicants ratio remained 1.18 and employment was higher than a year earlier, so the August data do not establish a broad labour contraction.
U.S. August hires were broadly stable and September payroll data were not yet available at the publication cutoff.
limitations: Eurostat's September HICP reading is a flash estimate; the full September release is scheduled for 16 October 2026.
National euro-area inflation comparisons use harmonised flash estimates and do not by themselves establish national real-income or wage conditions.
Japan's active job-openings ratio covers the public employment placement system and is not identical to an economy-wide vacancy rate.
Japan labour-force data refer to August and therefore lag the 2 October publication date.
The U.S. section intentionally excludes September payrolls, unemployment and wages because the BLS release is scheduled after the report cutoff.
The monetary-policy transmission chain is an analytical risk mechanism, not proof that energy inflation will pass through to wages, services or policy rates.
notes: Approved as a morning 2 October edition with a pre-payroll cutoff; any later U.S. Employment Situation evidence should enter as a subsequent evidence update, not be backfilled into the approved cutoff.

en.title: Global Macro — Euro-area inflation climbs to 3.8% as Japan labour demand softens ahead of U.S. payrolls
en.deck: Euro-area inflation accelerated to 3.8% as energy reached 18.8%; Japan unemployment rose to 2.5% while new job postings fell 3.4% year on year.
en.regime: Policy divergence under uneven inflation and labour constraints: euro-area price pressure has reaccelerated, Japan's vacancy flow is softening, and the U.S. labour picture awaits September payroll confirmation.
en.key_risk: If European energy inflation passes into services and wages while labour demand weakens elsewhere, major central banks may face increasingly different trade-offs between inflation persistence and employment momentum.

pt-BR.title: Macro Global — Inflação da área do euro sobe a 3,8% enquanto a demanda por trabalho no Japão perde força antes do emprego americano
pt-BR.deck: A inflação da área do euro acelerou para 3,8% e energia chegou a 18,8%; o desemprego japonês subiu a 2,5% enquanto novas vagas caíram 3,4% em doze meses.
pt-BR.regime: Divergência de política sob restrições diferentes de inflação e trabalho: a pressão de preços na área do euro reacelerou, o fluxo de vagas no Japão enfraquece e o quadro americano aguarda confirmação do payroll de setembro.
pt-BR.key_risk: Se a inflação de energia europeia se transmitir para serviços e salários enquanto a demanda por trabalho enfraquece em outras economias, grandes bancos centrais podem enfrentar trade-offs cada vez mais diferentes entre persistência inflacionária e emprego.
